entries.title: Fire from home
entries.literal_meaning: To tuck fire into the fold at one’s waist because it is the household’s fire.
entries.explanation: The reason offered is familiarity: the fire belongs to the house. The imagined act brings it against the body. Our reading questions treating something harmful as harmless merely because it is one’s own. The wording itself contains no explicit prohibition; this warning is our interpretation of the image.
entries.meaning_odia: କାରଣଟି ହେଉଛି ନିଜରପଣ—ନିଆଁଟି ଘରର। କିନ୍ତୁ ତାକୁ ଅଣ୍ଟିରେ ପୂରାଇବାର କଳ୍ପନା ଦେହ ପାଖକୁ ଆଣେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ନିଜର ବୋଲି କ୍ଷତିକାରକ ଜିନିଷକୁ ନିରାପଦ ଭାବିବା ନେଇ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଅଛି। ମୂଳ କଥାରେ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ନିଷେଧ ନାହିଁ; ସତର୍କତାଟି ଏହି ଛବିରୁ ଆମର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା।
entries.english_summary: Our reading questions the protection supposedly offered by calling a danger one’s own.
entries.odia_summary: ନିଜର ବୋଲି ବିପଦ ଦୂର ହୁଏ କି—ଆମ ପଢ଼ାର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ସମିତିର ନିଜ ଛାପାଖାନାରୁ ଆସିଥିବା ପତ୍ରିକାରେ ଭୁଲ ରହିଗଲା। ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “ନିଜ ଲୋକଙ୍କ କାମ, ଛାଡ଼ିଦିଅ।” ସମ୍ପାଦକ ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇ କହିଲେ, “ନିଜର ବୋଲି ଭୁଲଟି ଠିକ୍ ହୋଇଯିବନି।” / A committee newsletter contains an error. Someone says to overlook it because their own printer made it. The editor recalls the saying: “Being ours does not make the mistake right.” This exchange is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The entry also lists family secrets as a separate sense. It supplies no domestic incident or family-abuse gloss for the quotation. The publication example is editorial, not collected usage.

entries.odia: ଶାହି ଶାହି ହୋଇ ବୁଲଇ ଗୋରସ, ମଦ ବିକାଯାଏ ବସି
entries.title: One goes round, one stays put
entries.literal_meaning: Milk goes from neighbourhood to neighbourhood; liquor is sold while sitting.
entries.explanation: Movement belongs to the milk; sitting belongs to the liquor sale. The contrast makes unequal selling effort visible. Our reading uses that imbalance to ask why one offering must seek attention while another receives it. The source does not explain the difference or supply evidence about actual demand.
entries.meaning_odia: ବୁଲିବାଟି ଗୋରସ ସହ, ବସି ବିକିବାଟି ମଦ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ବିକ୍ରିର ଦୁଇ ଭିନ୍ନ ପରିଶ୍ରମ ଏହି ବିରୋଧରେ ଦିଶେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠେ—ଗୋଟିଏ ଜିନିଷକୁ ଧ୍ୟାନ ପାଇବାକୁ ଖୋଜି ବୁଲିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ୁଛି, ଅନ୍ୟଟି ପାଖକୁ ଲୋକ ଆସୁଛନ୍ତି କାହିଁକି? ଏହି କାରଣ ବା ପ୍ରକୃତ ଚାହିଦାର ତଥ୍ୟ ଉତ୍ସ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Contrasting selling effort prompts our question about uneven attention.
entries.odia_summary: ବିକ୍ରିର ଭିନ୍ନ ପରିଶ୍ରମରେ ଅସମାନ ଧ୍ୟାନକୁ ନେଇ ଆମ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପଢ଼ାଚକ୍ର ପାଇଁ ନିମନ୍ତ୍ରଣ ନେଇ ସଦସ୍ୟମାନେ ଘରେ ଘରେ ଯାଉଥିଲେ। ପାଖରେ ଏକ ଖେଳ ପ୍ରତିଯୋଗିତାକୁ ଲୋକ ନିଜେ ଆସୁଥିଲେ। ଜଣେ ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇ ପଚାରିଲେ, “ଆମ ନିମନ୍ତ୍ରଣରେ କଣ ବଦଳାଇବା?” / Reading-group members deliver invitations door to door while a nearby game attracts visitors on its own. One recalls the line and asks, “What should we change in our invitation?” This comparison is invented, not a ranking of the activities.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary defines the repeated neighbourhood expression, not a historical trading custom. No virtue ranking, universal consumer preference or health claim is inferred.

entries.odia: ବୋହି ଗଲା ପାଣି ଯାଉ ତେଣିକି, ବନ୍ଧେଇଲା ପାଣି ରହୁ ଅଟକି
entries.title: What has flowed, what remains
entries.literal_meaning: Let the water that has flowed away go that way; let the dammed water remain held.
entries.explanation: The two wishes face different water: what has already gone and what can remain contained. Our reading turns attention from recovering every loss to keeping what is still available. This is an editorial application of the contrast, not a promise that every loss can be repaired by restraint.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦୁଇଟି ଇଚ୍ଛା ଦୁଇ ଅବସ୍ଥାର ପାଣିକୁ ନେଇ—ଯାହା ବୋହିଗଲା ଓ ଯାହା ଅଟକି ରହିଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ହରାଇଥିବା ଜିନିଷ ଫେରାଇବାଠାରୁ ଧ୍ୟାନ ଏବେ ଥିବା ଜିନିଷକୁ ରଖିବା ଆଡ଼କୁ ଫେରେ। ଏହା ବିରୋଧଟିର ଆମର ପ୍ରୟୋଗ; ସଂଯମରେ ସବୁ କ୍ଷତି ଭରଣା ହେବ ବୋଲି ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading distinguishes a past loss from what can still be kept.
entries.odia_summary: ବିତିଥିବା କ୍ଷତି ଓ ରଖିପାରିବା ଜିନିଷ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଆମ ପଢ଼ାର ତଫାତ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ବର୍ଷାରେ ପଢ଼ାଚକ୍ରର ଗୋଟିଏ ଦିନ ବାତିଲ ହେଲା। ଆୟୋଜକ ସେଦିନକୁ ନେଇ ଅନୁତାପ କରୁଥିବାବେଳେ ସାଙ୍ଗ ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇ କହିଲେ, “ଆସନ୍ତା ଦୁଇଦିନର ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥା କରିବା।” / Rain cancels one day of a reading programme. While an organiser regrets it, a friend recalls the saying: “Let us arrange the two days still ahead.” This application is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The verb’s dam-building sense supports the water image. No particular river, engineering method, conservation custom or practical water-management instruction is documented here.

entries.odia: ଛୋଟ ମୁହଁରେ ବଡ଼ କଥା, ଶୁଣିଲା ଲୋକର ମନ ବ୍ୟଥା
entries.title: Whose words cause offence?
entries.literal_meaning: Big words from a small mouth: the listener’s mind is hurt.
entries.explanation: The dictionary’s “small” marks a person treated as low or insignificant. The line places the listener’s hurt beside that person’s speech. Our critical reading asks whether the offence comes from the words or from refusing the speaker standing. That question challenges the hierarchy; it is not a tolerant moral supplied by the saying.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ “ଛୋଟ” କଥାଟି ନୀଚ ବା ନଗଣ୍ୟ ବୋଲି ଧରାଯାଇଥିବା ମଣିଷକୁ ସୂଚାଏ। ସେ ମଣିଷର କଥା ପାଖରେ ଶ୍ରୋତାର ମନବ୍ୟଥା ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଆମର ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ାରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ—କଥାଟି ବାଧିଲା, ନା କହୁଥିବା ଲୋକକୁ ମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦା ଦେବାର ଅନିଚ୍ଛା? ଏହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଚ୍ଚନୀଚ ବିଚାର ଉପରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠାଏ; ଢଗଟି ନିଜେ ସହନଶୀଳତାର ନୀତି ଶିଖାଉଛି ବୋଲି କୁହାଯାଉନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical reading separates a speaker’s standing from the worth of the words.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ାରେ ବକ୍ତାର ସ୍ଥାନ ଓ କଥାର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଅଲଗା।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ନୂଆ ସଦସ୍ୟ ହିସାବର ଏକ ଭୁଲ ଦେଖାଇଲେ। ଜଣେ ଢଗଟି କହି ତାଙ୍କୁ ଚୁପ୍ କରାଇବାକୁ ଚାହିଁଲେ। ସଭାପତି କହିଲେ, “ସେ କେତେଦିନର ସଦସ୍ୟ, ତାହା ନୁହେଁ; ହିସାବଟି ମେଳୁଛି କି ଦେଖିବା।” / A newcomer points out an accounting error. Someone invokes the saying to silence them. The chair replies, “Their membership is recent; let us still check the figures.” This critical exchange is invented.
entries.cultural_context: Historical rank language is retained as source evidence, not a judgment of anyone’s worth. The source identifies no caste, age, gender or particular speaker in the quotation.
